verdict: Ares' revenue fell 14% to $1.43B because carried interest dropped by two-thirds from a strong quarter last year, even as management fees hit a record $1.06B; fee related earnings were $524M.

kpis.label: Management fees
kpis.note: A record, +9% vs a year ago

kpis.label: Total revenues
kpis.note: -14% vs a year ago on lower carried interest

kpis.label: Fee related earnings
kpis.note: Ares' preferred measure of recurring profit

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP, attributable)
kpis.note: After-tax realized income was $1.26 per share

segments.name: Management fees
segments.note: Recurring fees for managing credit, private equity, real estate and other funds — the steady core of the business.

segments.name: Carried interest allocation
segments.note: Ares' share of fund profits — lumpy by nature, and well below a strong quarter a year ago.

segments.name: Incentive fees
segments.note: Performance fees from publicly traded and perpetual funds.

segments.name: Principal investment income
segments.note: Returns on Ares' own money invested alongside clients.

opex.name: Performance-related compensation
opex.note: The share of carried interest paid out to the investment teams who earned it.

opex.name: Expenses of Consolidated Funds
opex.note: Operating costs of funds Ares consolidates for accounting purposes.

otherDetail: Losses of $147M on Ares' own investments and $59M of interest expense, partly offset by gains and income inside consolidated funds (a net $168M) and $9M of interest and dividend income.

takeaways.title: Management fees hit a record $1.06B
takeaways.text: The recurring fee base keeps growing with assets under management, even in a quarter when performance income faded.

takeaways.title: Carried interest fell to $162M
takeaways.text: Profit-sharing from funds dropped by two-thirds versus an unusually strong quarter a year ago, pulling total revenue down 14%.

takeaways.title: Fee related earnings of $524M
takeaways.text: On the recurring measure Ares emphasizes, earnings stayed strong; GAAP net income attributable to the listed company was $85M after sharing profits with fund investors and operating-group partners.

footerNote: Compensation and benefits is treated as the direct cost of an asset manager (the people who generate the fees). Consolidated net income of $205M is shown; from it, $77M belonged to investors in consolidated funds and $43M to operating-group partners, leaving $85M attributable to Ares Management Corporation shareholders.
